verdict.rationale: Blaxel documents configurable expiration policies that automatically delete sandboxes on conditions such as inactivity or TTL, which is a narrow product-native rule-to-action mechanism. Its schedules run commands on time-based triggers (cron, a future datetime, or a delay), but these are time triggers rather than event-driven rules. missing for 10: general user-defined event-to-action rules (e.g. on file change, process exit, or deploy), a choice of actions beyond deletion, any event/trigger model documentation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Configure expiration policies to automatically delete Blaxel sandboxes after inactivity, a TTL, or other conditions
Run a command inside a Blaxel sandbox on a recurring cron schedule, a future datetime, or after a delay, with execution history per run.
